_about: Shot structures: how an ad is filmed and cut, picked per video from what its script argues (ad-brief-compiler section 2). A video's format (templates/formats.json) is the argument; its structure is the camera and the edit. Each: what it is, which arguments it serves, the 8 scene rows (A01-B04, [size, move, what the row shows]; 'argued' has one map per format), the edit's pace, whether the punchline gets the 1.15 zoom and a Slide Blur ('transitions': [] for none; left out = the format's), whether the size must change at every cut (cut_sheet.py prints SAME SIZE), and the risk to write against. Every structure fits Negen's Conversion Creative V3 skill, which cuts each 10 s part into about three shots with real cuts and wants a visible event in the first 1-2 s: no structure is one continuous take, and none opens on a static beauty shot or a slow decorative push-in. An explore group uses at least two structures across V1-V3; an iterate group keeps the control's unless structure is its variable.

argued.name: Argued cuts
argued.idea: each sentence its own shot size and camera move, the shot proving what the sentence says; the size changes at every cut
argued.fits: turn, myth, list, after: an argument with a problem, a turn and reasons to show
argued.pace: one or two shots a sentence, a hard cut to a new size on every sentence
argued.risk: close-ups of a sculptural product drift: keep where the part meets the rest in frame

follow.name: Follow, cut on action
follow.idea: one lived moment with one person, filmed handheld and cut on action: every cut carries on the movement of the shot before (she sets the cup down, cut, her hand lets go, cut, she sits back), the size stepping wide, medium, close as she reaches the product; about three shots a part, never one continuous take
follow.fits: story, ritual: a lived moment, first person, the product as part of the day
follow.pace: cut on action: one shot a sentence, each cut continuing the movement before it; no punch zoom, no Slide Blur
follow.risk: Negen's Conversion Creative V3 rejects a part that is one continuous camera move: write separate rows joined by the action, never 'one take'; one long action also lets people and the product drift, so every row repeats ACTOR A's clothes and the product's outline and place
rows: hook event: ACTOR A already doing something with the product in the first second (sets a cup down, drops onto the seat)
the same movement carried on, the room around them
their hand on the part the sentence names, body in frame
the action carried on as they settle (A04 ends mid-action)
B01 continues A04's action from the same state, a detail of it
ACTOR A at home with it, the room around

tableau.name: Still-life tableaux
tableau.idea: an event on the hook, then composed, calm frames like a catalogue page in a lived room: the product centred, ACTOR A stepping into and out of frame, slow slides and push-ins, the light doing the work; a hard cut between frames
tableau.fits: gift, aspiration, a premium piece, an offer-led ad: the piece as something worth owning
tableau.pace: an event on the hook, then one composed shot a sentence, clean hard cuts, no zoom
tableau.risk: Negen's Conversion Creative V3 rejects a static beauty shot or a slow decorative push-in as the opening: the hook is an event (ACTOR A sets the piece's last object in place, steps into frame), the calm frames come after; near-still frames also make Negen copy the poster, so every row names a slow move and ACTOR A moves
rows: hook event: ACTOR A sets something on the product or steps into the frame beside it in the first second
the room composed around the product
the piece itself, centred, outline in frame
ACTOR A beside it for scale
the product whole, ACTOR A stepping out of frame

pov.name: First-person
pov.idea: the camera is ACTOR A's eyes at standing or sitting height: the viewer does what they do (sets the cup down, reaches for the book); their own hands come in from the bottom edge at waist or table height
pov.fits: ritual, list, story: use and convenience, what it is like to live with it
pov.pace: one or two shots a sentence, cuts on the hand actions
pov.risk: hands: only from the bottom edge to waist or table height (section 6); ACTOR A is seen whole only in a mirror-free WIDE or the end frame
rows: hook event: ACTOR A's own hands set something on the product in the first second, the room ahead
the problem or moment in front of them, their hands at table height
their hand sets something on the product
the top and what sits on it, their hand reaching
they sit or step back: the product beside them
ACTOR A seen whole beside it for scale

match.name: Before/after match cuts
match.idea: the same framing twice: the room without the product, then a hard cut to the identical frame with it; the change is the punchline
match.fits: after, turn, myth: a visible change to the room
match.pace: hold the before, a hard match cut on the turn, then the argued rows
match.risk: the model plays two framings in reverse or dissolves them (section 1): the before and the after are separate rows (A02, A03), the framing written in the same words in both
rows: hook event: ACTOR A in the before-room, doing something the problem gets in the way of
the before: the wall or corner without our product, framing named exactly
the after: the identical frame, our product in it (hard cut)
the part that made the difference
ACTOR A beside it for scale

montage.name: Detail montage
montage.idea: quick beats of 1-1.5 s on details and uses, a cut on every beat, building to the product whole
montage.fits: list: many reasons, comparing buyers; a product with several features to show
montage.pace: two or three shots a sentence, a hard cut on every beat
montage.risk: many close-ups mean more drift: every close row keeps the outline in frame, and the shot check is strict on them
rows: the promise, on an event: ACTOR A already using the product in the first second
detail two: the top in use
detail three: its height or base
a hand using it, body in frame
